when.quote: Procedure for when a customer wants to close, cancel, or deactivate their debit card.

starts.note: agent: after filing debit disputes, the agent must perform each card's most severe mapped action (freeze or close), based only on the disputes actually filed. A card whose filed disputes all map to keep_active is left alone, even if another dispute on it was held back. The customer may also start this job by asking to close or cancel a card (lost, stolen, fraud, damaged, no longer needed, account closing). Order a replacement only if the customer wants one. Never close a card the customer says they found and want to keep.
starts.quote: This parameter records metadata only; the agent must separately perform the indicated card action after filing the dispute.

tools.not_used: Unfreezing is only for a customer who asks to unfreeze a FROZEN card. Acting on disputes or closing a card never unfreezes one.
Disputes are filed in filing_a_debit_card_transaction_dispute, before this job.
The credit card check after a lost or stolen card belongs to lost_stolen_card_cross_product_security_protocol (cross_product_handoff).
Doc 005 is cited only for its tier list. No account is closed here.
The fraud alert on a card closed after a fraud dispute is not cleared (alert_card_not_cleared). The card is closed instead.

steps.do: If the customer was not verified earlier in this conversation, verify them first: look them up by name, email or id, check that 2 of DOB, email, phone and address match, call get_current_time, then log_verification. Otherwise reuse the verified user.
steps.quote: Customer must be verified

steps.do: Unlock get_debit_dispute_status_7483, then call it to read the disputes filed in this conversation and their categories per card.
steps.if: the job follows disputes filed in this conversation
steps.quote: To retrieve a customer's debit card dispute history and check the status of open disputes, use the get_debit_dispute_status_7483 tool.

steps.do: Unlock get_debit_cards_by_account_id_7823, then call it for each affected checking account to read card_id, user_id, status, date_issued and issue_reason.
steps.quote: Use get_debit_cards_by_account_id_7823 to look up all debit cards associated with a specific checking account.

steps.do: Unlock get_bank_account_transactions_9173, then call it for each affected account to find any transactions with status pending.
steps.quote: Transaction status, either 'posted' or 'pending'

steps.do: Unlock get_all_user_accounts_by_user_id_3847, then call it to read each account's class (tier), status and balance.
steps.quote: Use get_all_user_accounts_by_user_id_3847 to retrieve the bank accounts (checkings, savings) for a customer.

steps.do: Get the current time for the card-age, 12-month and 48-hour checks.
steps.quote: Minimum card age: The debit card must have been active for at least 14 days.

steps.do: For each card with filed disputes, take the most severe card_action among its disputes: close_and_reissue > freeze_pending_investigation > keep_active. Perform the chosen action once per card. Each card is decided on its own disputes, so one card may stay active while another is closed. A customer request to close a lost or stolen card also means closing it. If the customer asks for the card to be replaced because of fraud, close it with reason fraud_suspected.
steps.if: the job follows disputes filed in this conversation
steps.quote: Severity order (highest to lowest): 'close_and_reissue' > 'freeze_pending_investigation' > 'keep_active'.

steps.do: Leave out any dispute the customer raised but did not file (for example one held back by the open-dispute limit): it sets no card action. If the card's filed disputes all map to keep_active, the card stays active. Do not offer a freeze or closure for it unless the customer asks.
steps.if: a dispute on the card was held back and not filed
steps.quote: However, when performing the actual card action after filing all disputes, use the MOST SEVERE action across all disputes.

steps.do: A card that has a customer-initiated fraud alert and a filed fraud dispute (close_and_reissue) is closed as it is. Do not clear its alert first, because the customer did not confirm every transaction. Close it with reason fraud_suspected through check_elig and close.
steps.if: the card's fraud_alert_active is TRUE and its most severe filed dispute action is close_and_reissue
steps.quote: If they confirm all transactions are legitimate, clear the alert.

steps.do: Tell the customer the card stays active and no action is needed.
steps.if: the most severe action is keep_active and the customer did not ask to close the card
steps.quote: 'duplicate_charge' → 'keep_active'

steps.do: If the customer says one of the cards was not lost after all (they found it), do not close it, because a closed card can never be reopened. If it was frozen and they want it back, unfreeze it in freezing_and_unfreezing_a_debit_card. Close only the cards still confirmed lost or stolen.
steps.if: the customer says a card they reported is no longer missing
steps.quote: Closed cards cannot be reopened - customer must order a new card if needed

steps.do: Ask for, or confirm, the closure reason for each card being closed: lost, stolen, fraud_suspected, damaged, no_longer_needed or account_closing. A card the customer lost or had stolen uses lost or stolen. A card closed because of fraud disputes otherwise uses fraud_suspected.
steps.quote: 2. Ask customer for the reason they want to close the card (select from: lost, stolen, fraud_suspected, damaged, no_longer_needed, account_closing)

steps.do:
Check five things:
1. The card's user_id matches the verified user.
2. Its status is ACTIVE or PENDING.
3. It has no pending transactions.
4. It has no pending refunds.
5. It has been active at least 14 days (skipped for lost, stolen or fraud_suspected).
If a check fails, tell the customer what must be resolved (for example, wait for pending transactions to settle, or the earliest date the card can be closed) and do not close.
steps.quote: These reasons bypass the minimum card age requirement (requirement 6) for security purposes

steps.do: Tell the customer that pending transactions will still be processed, and ask whether they want a replacement card now. If fraud is suspected, advise them to review recent transactions and dispute any unauthorized charges.
steps.if: the reason is lost, stolen or fraud_suspected
steps.quote: Inform customer that any pending transactions will still be processed

steps.do: Unlock close_debit_card_4721, then close each card with its reason from ask_reason.

args.reason: from ask_reason: lost, stolen, fraud_suspected (the default for fraud disputes), or the reason the customer gave

steps.if: check_elig passed AND (the customer asked to close the card OR pick_action gave close_and_reissue)
steps.quote: 5. Use close_debit_card_4721 to close the card with parameters: card_id, reason

steps.do: A card the customer froze earlier in this same conversation, and now confirms stolen or lost and asks to cancel, shows status FROZEN. Do not unfreeze a stolen card first. If checks 1, 3 and 4 of check_elig pass, call close_debit_card_4721 for it with reason stolen or lost. If the tool rejects it because of the status, explain this to the customer and handle it under action_error. (The documents do not cover this case; see open_questions.)

args.reason: stolen or lost, as the customer said

steps.if: the card is FROZEN because the customer froze it earlier in this conversation over the same loss or theft, the customer now asks to cancel it, and checks 1, 3 and 4 passed
steps.quote: Cards reported as lost or stolen are closed immediately with no cooling-off period

steps.do: Confirm three things: the card is permanently deactivated and cannot be reactivated; recurring payments on it must be updated; a new card can be ordered. For a fraud_suspected closure, recommend changing the online banking password.
steps.if: close succeeded
steps.quote: The card is now permanently deactivated and cannot be reactivated

steps.do: Check that the card's status is ACTIVE and that it belongs to the verified user. If the customer says the card is lost or stolen, recommend closing it instead.
steps.if: the most severe action is freeze_pending_investigation
steps.quote: If customer confirms the card is lost/stolen, recommend closing instead of freezing

steps.do: Tell the customer three things: new transactions and recurring payments will be declined while the card is frozen; authorized pending transactions may still process; they can unfreeze at any time. Then unlock freeze_debit_card_3892, freeze the card, and confirm it succeeded.
steps.if: the most severe action is freeze_pending_investigation and the card is ACTIVE (freeze_check passed)
steps.quote: Use freeze_debit_card_3892 with the card_id

steps.do: Ask whether the customer wants a replacement card now.
steps.if: the card was closed
steps.quote: Ask if they want to order a replacement card immediately

steps.do:
Check ordering eligibility and the tier rules:
1. The account is an OPEN checking account with a balance of at least $25.
2. There is no other ACTIVE or PENDING card on it.
3. Count the cards with issue_reason lost, stolen, fraud or damaged issued in the last 12 months, against the tier limit: Entry 2 (or a $25 excess fee), Mid 3 (or a $15 excess fee), Premium 5 (then wait), Elite unlimited.
If the customer is not eligible, explain what blocks the order and do not order.
steps.if: the customer wants a replacement
steps.quote: 3) Check the date_issued field and count cards issued within the last 12 months

steps.do: For an Entry-tier account (Light Blue, Light Green, Green Fee-Free), tell the customer a replacement can be ordered only 48 hours after the closure. Give the earliest time, and do not order now.
steps.if: the account is Entry tier and less than 48 hours have passed since the closure
steps.quote: 48-hour waiting period after card closure before a replacement can be ordered

steps.do:
Explain the tier's delivery and design fees:
- Delivery: Entry STANDARD $0 only; Mid STANDARD $0, EXPEDITED $15; Premium STANDARD or EXPEDITED $0, RUSH $35; Elite all $0.
- Design: Entry and Mid CLASSIC $0, PREMIUM $10, CUSTOM $25; Premium $0, $0 and $15; Elite all $0.
Ask for the customer's choices, confirm the mailing address, and say any fee is deducted from the checking account. If the customer wants the best free option, choose the best options that cost $0 at their tier.
steps.if: replacement_check passed and no Entry-tier wait applies
steps.quote: Always inform the customer that the fee will be deducted from their checking account balance before placing the order.

steps.do: If the customer asks for the best free options, pick the highest-value $0 choices for the tier: Premium (Evergreen) EXPEDITED shipping and the PREMIUM design, both $0; Elite RUSH and any design, all $0; Mid and Entry STANDARD and CLASSIC. Tell the customer what was chosen and that no fee applies.
steps.if: the customer asks for the best free options for their tier
steps.quote: PREMIUM design (metallic silver): design_fee $0 (complimentary)

steps.do: If the customer wants the card mailed somewhere other than the address on file (for example a work address), take the full address, check that it is a US domestic address, read it back, and use it as the order's address.
steps.if: the customer gives a mailing address other than the one on file
steps.quote: Confirm the address that the customer would like to mail the card to.

steps.do: Unlock order_debit_card_5739 and order the replacement with the exact tier fees, using the parameter names the unlock reports.

arguments.address: as confirmed (the address on file or the alternate address)

steps.if: the customer wants a replacement, replacement_check passed, the tier's waiting period has passed, and the customer confirmed the options and fees
steps.quote: When using order_debit_card_5739, you must provide the exact delivery_fee and design_fee amounts based on the tier rules below.

steps.do: Tell the customer the expected delivery time (STANDARD 7-10, EXPEDITED 3-5, RUSH 1-2 business days) and any fees. If the order failed (for example, insufficient funds for the fees), explain why.
steps.quote: 8) Inform customer of expected delivery timeframe and any applicable fees

steps.do: If the card was closed or frozen because it was lost or stolen, run lost_stolen_card_cross_product_security_protocol next.
steps.if: the card was reported lost or stolen
steps.quote: Complete the standard debit card freeze/close procedure

steps.do: If a close, freeze or order call returns an error, explain that the action could not be completed and why. If it cannot be resolved, offer a transfer to a human agent (technical_system_error), and transfer only if the customer agrees.

steps.if: a close, freeze or order call returns an error that cannot be resolved and the customer agrees to a transfer
steps.quote: System error or outage preventing completion of the customer's request

done_when: Each card the customer asked to close, and each card with filed disputes, has had its action performed (kept active, frozen, or closed with the right reason) and confirmed, or the customer was told what blocks it. Disputes that were not filed set no card action. A card with a fraud alert and a filed fraud dispute was closed without its alert being cleared. A card the customer found again was not closed. For each closed card, one of these is true: a replacement was ordered to the confirmed address (on file or alternate) with the correct tier fees and timeframe; the customer declined one; or the customer was told when one can be ordered (the Entry 48-hour wait or the tier limit). Lost and stolen cards have been handed to the cross-product check.
